issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares ExcellenceLand.excellencyLevel as type double, but the solution implementation declares excellencyLevel as int. This mismatch affects the constructor parameter type and the getter return type, causing confusion and potential test failures when students implement the class according to the UML.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the attribute types consistent with the UML: change ExcellenceLand.excellencyLevel to double in the implementation, update the constructor parameter to double, and update the getter to return double. Alternatively, update the UML/problem statement to specify int if that was intended.
